chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Ubaydah and al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He was asked about a man who killed a woman accidentally while she was in labor giving birth to a child. He said: Upon him is five hundred thousand dirhams, and upon him is the blood money of what is in her womb: a head payment (ghurrah), or a young slave, or a young female slave, or forty dinars. There is no contradiction between these narrations and the earlier ones, because the earlier ones are interpreted as referring to a fetus that has completed its formation and matured, except that the soul has not yet entered it. And this one is interpreted as referring to a woman who expels a clot (alaqah) or a chewed piece of flesh (mudghah), so the blood money for that is a head payment (for a male or female slave) or a young slave/slave, and that which indicates this.

key_terms.دِيَة: Blood money or compensation for death/injury
key_terms.رَأْسُ الْوَلَدِ: Head of the child, indicating the stage of labor/birth
key_terms.عَلَقَةً: A clot of blood, an early stage of fetal development
key_terms.غُرَّةٌ: A head payment, typically for a slave or a specific stage of fetal development
key_terms.مُضْغَةً: A chewed piece of flesh, a later stage of fetal development before bone formation

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money for a fetus in the womb if the mother is killed accidentally?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction between differing hadiths by distinguishing between a fetus that has reached full physical formation but lacks the soul (requiring the higher 500,000 dirham compensation) and one in an earlier embryonic stage of 'alaqah or mudghah (requiring the lower ghurrah or 40 dinars). This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the degree of fetal development directly dictates the magnitude of the blood money, reflecting a nuanced understanding of biological stages in legal rulings.
